output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs comes mainly from inside the DC, not from Haverlow. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four on 27 July, chilled pallets wait about 3 h 52 min on average between unload and reaching a chamber, up from 44 min. They sit on an unrefrigerated dock at 15–17°C. Night-shift write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier. Day-shift rates barely moved. Haverlow's trailer records show 1.9–3.6°C on every load, and doors were closed about 40 minutes after opening. The 6.5–8°C receiving probe readings were taken after the pallets had warmed on the dock, so they don't show a supplier fault. The chambers held temperature. I'm quite confident in this, so don't raise the chargeback or shift volume. Restore night receiving staffing, or otherwise get chilled pallets into chambers quickly, and set a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored weekly. Don't drop the probe. Corriebank's self-certified credits probably explain a smaller part of the rise, and that's unproven. Request their claim-level data and check a sample before changing their terms.
